stem: Before positioning a patient for a finger radiograph, which action is listed in the preparation notes?
options: Select exposure factors without speaking to the patient
Leave all materials around the fingers
Begin exposure before explaining the procedure
quote: Proper identification
explanation: The preparation list begins with proper identification. The same slide also requires explanation, reassurance and removal of materials around the fingers and hand.

stem: For the dorsipalmar finger projection, which surface should contact the film?
options: Lateral aspect of the thumb only
quote: Place palmar aspect of the fingers under examination on film
explanation: The palmar aspect of the examined fingers is placed on the film. The fingers are separated slightly and the hand and wrist immobilized as described on this slide.

stem: A student is positioning fingers for the PA projection. Which adjustment follows the lecture?
options: Cross the fingers over one another
Flex every finger into the palm
quote: Separate fingers slightly
explanation: The PA positioning instructions specify slight finger separation. This question tests the arrangement stated in the supplied lecture.

stem: Where is the central ray centred for the PA finger projection in the lecture?
options: Proximal interphalangeal joint of the examined finger
quote: CP: At the level of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the fingers or finger under examination.
explanation: The stated centring point is the proximal interphalangeal joint of the finger under examination. Use this slide to distinguish finger centring from hand and elbow centring.

stem: For a lateral projection of the ring and little fingers, which border of the hand is placed on the film?
quote: From the PA position, the medial border of the hand is place on the film
explanation: The lateral ring-and-little-finger instructions place the medial border of the hand on the film. The same section calls for extension and separation of those fingers.

stem: Which support is specified for the ring finger during its lateral projection?
quote: Support ring finger with foam pad
explanation: The lecture specifies a foam pad to support the ring finger. It separately instructs flexion of the other fingers.

stem: A lateral finger image omits the fingertip. Which coverage requirement in the lecture has been missed?
options: Include the fingertip and distal third of the metacarpal
quote: NOTE: The image should include the tip of the finger and distal 3rd of the metacarpal
explanation: The lecture explicitly requires the fingertip and distal third of the metacarpal. An image missing the fingertip does not meet that stated coverage requirement.

stem: Where is the PA thumb projection centred in the supplied lecture?
options: Proximal interphalangeal joint of the little finger
quote: CP: Metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb
explanation: The PA thumb section identifies the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint as its centring point. This differs from the proximal interphalangeal centring described for fingers.

stem: Which part of the hand should be protected from exerted pressure during the PA thumb positioning described?
quote: Avoid exerting pressure on thenar eminence
explanation: The thumb positioning instructions explicitly say to avoid exerting pressure on the thenar eminence. This is a stated positioning precaution in the source.

stem: In the PA thumb notes, what adjustment compensates for a large object-to-film distance?
quote: NOTE: Increase the FFD to compensate for the large OFD
explanation: The lecture instructs increasing FFD to compensate for the large OFD. The question asks for the adjustment given in these notes.

stem: For the mediolateral thumb projection, which aspect of the thumb contacts the cassette?
quote: The lateral aspect of the thumb is in contact with the cassette
explanation: The mediolateral thumb instructions specify lateral thumb contact with the cassette. The fingers are partially flexed and supported on a foam pad in this positioning description.

stem: During PA hand positioning, how should the radial and ulnar styloid processes relate to the cassette?
options: They should be equidistant from it
Only the ulnar styloid should touch it
Both should be outside the field
quote: The wrist is adjusted so that the ulnar and radius styloid processes are equidistant from the cassette
explanation: The PA hand description requires the styloid processes to be equidistant from the cassette. Superimposition is described for a different, lateral position in this deck.

stem: A student centres a PA hand radiograph. Which landmark is specified in the lecture?
quote: CP: Over the head of the THIRD metacarpal
explanation: The PA hand centring point is over the head of the third metacarpal. Read the PA section of this slide, before its separate oblique-position instructions.

stem: How much external rotation is specified when moving from a PA hand to a PA oblique hand?
quote: From the PA position, the hand is externally rotated 45 degrees with fingers extended
explanation: The lecture specifies 45 degrees of external rotation with the fingers extended. It also describes a 45-degree foam pad to support the position.

stem: Which relationship of the styloid processes is required for the lateral hand position?
options: Styloids equidistant with the palm flat
Radial styloid excluded from the image
Ulnar styloid excluded from the image
quote: The radial and ulnar styloid processes are superimposed
explanation: The lateral hand instructions require superimposition of the radial and ulnar styloid processes. This provides a source-based check of the stated positioning.

stem: What purpose does the lecture specifically associate with the lateral hand projection?
quote: Note: This projection is commonly done to identify the foreign bodies.
explanation: The note under lateral hand positioning identifies foreign-body detection as a common purpose. No additional indication is needed to answer this question.

stem: For the ball-catcher position, how are both hands rotated from the initial supinated position?
quote: From this position, both hands are rotated medially 45 degree into a Ball-catching position
explanation: The ball-catcher description specifies medial rotation of both hands by 45 degrees. This is distinct from the externally rotated single-hand oblique position.

stem: For the PA wrist projection, what centring point is given?
options: Midway between radial and ulnar styloid processes
quote: CP: Midway between the ulnar and radial styloid processes
explanation: The PA wrist instructions centre midway between the radial and ulnar styloid processes. The slide places the palm, wrist and lower forearm in a straight line.

stem: Why is a small pad placed under the metacarpophalangeal joints for the PA wrist in these notes?
options: To maintain close wrist contact with the film
To raise the wrist away from the film
To rotate the elbow through 90 degrees
quote: Place small pad under metacarpophalangeal joints of hand to maintain wrist in close contact with film
explanation: The stated purpose of the pad is close wrist contact with the film. The question directly tests the purpose supplied in the positioning instructions.

stem: A student is checking a lateral wrist position. Which alignment is required by the notes?
options: Superimposed ulnar and radial styloid processes
Palm flat with no forearm rotation
quote: Ensure ulnar and radial styloid processes are superimposed
explanation: The lateral wrist instructions require superimposed styloid processes. This is the alignment check stated on the source slide.

stem: Which centring landmark is stated for the lateral wrist projection?
quote: CP:  Radial styloid processes
explanation: The lateral wrist section identifies the radial styloid as the centring landmark. The PA wrist section on the preceding slide uses the midpoint between the styloids.

stem: Which hand movement is specified in the PA scaphoid projection?
quote: Rest palm, wrist and lower forearm on the film with ulnar deviation of hand
explanation: The scaphoid projection described in the lecture uses ulnar deviation of the hand. This question concerns positioning rather than the separate follow-up timing note.

stem: Where is the superoinferior axial carpal-tunnel projection centred in the lecture?
quote: CP: Midcarpal region
explanation: The carpal-tunnel section gives the midcarpal region as its centring point. It also asks that the carpal region be placed in profile.

stem: For an AP forearm projection, what forearm and elbow positions are described?
options: Fully supinated forearm with elbow extended
Pronated forearm with elbow fully flexed
True lateral forearm with elbow at 90 degrees
quote: Place forearm fully supinated with elbow extended
explanation: The AP forearm instructions specify full supination and elbow extension. The lateral forearm instructions on the next slide describe a different elbow position.

stem: Which two joints should be included if possible on the AP forearm image?
quote: Include wrist and elbow if possible using long cassette size
explanation: The AP forearm notes ask for inclusion of both wrist and elbow where possible, using a long cassette. This is the source's stated image-coverage check.

stem: For the lateral forearm projection, what elbow flexion is described?
quote: Flex elbow at 90 degrees
explanation: The lateral forearm instructions specify 90 degrees of elbow flexion. This contrasts with the extended elbow described for the AP forearm.

stem: Where is the lateral forearm projection centred?
options: Lateral forearm midway between wrist and elbow
quote: CP: Lateral aspect of the forearm, midway between wrist and elbow joints
explanation: The stated lateral forearm centring point is halfway between the wrist and elbow on the lateral aspect. Both joints are also to be included if possible.

stem: Where is the AP elbow projection centred according to the lecture?
options: In the midline 2.5 cm distal to the epicondylar line
At the head of the third metacarpal
In the midline 5 cm proximal to the shoulder
quote: CP: In the midline 2.5cm distal to a line joining the lateral and medial epicondyles of the humerus
explanation: The AP elbow centring point is 2.5 cm distal to the line joining the humeral epicondyles. The distance and reference line are both explicitly stated.

stem: Which forearm position is described for the AP elbow projection?
options: Fully supinated with the elbow extended
Fully pronated with elbow at 90 degrees
Lateral with the elbow fully flexed
Hand resting on the opposite shoulder
quote: Place forearm fully supinated with elbow extended on a film
explanation: The AP elbow instructions require full forearm supination with the elbow extended. This identifies the position described on the AP elbow slide.

stem: When setting up the lateral elbow, which structures should be at the same level?
quote: Seat the patient alongside the X-ray couch with shoulder, elbow and hand at the same level.
explanation: The lateral elbow description places shoulder, elbow and hand at one level. The next instruction specifies 90-degree elbow flexion and a true lateral forearm.

stem: Which centring point is given for the lateral elbow projection?
quote: CP: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
explanation: The lateral elbow centring landmark is the lateral humeral epicondyle. This is explicitly different from the AP elbow's midline point below the epicondylar line.

stem: How is the elbow flexed for the axial elbow position described in the notes?
options: Until the hand contacts the shoulder
Until the palm lies flat beside the hip
With the arm kept fully extended
quote: Flex elbow so that the hand is in contact with the shoulder
explanation: The axial elbow instructions call for flexion until the hand contacts the shoulder. The elbow then rests on the film with the upper arm at couch level.

stem: Which listed factor influences the choice of exposure factors in the lecture?
options: Time printed on the appointment card
quote:
NOTE: The choice of exposure factors depends on
Anatomical structure
Type of film material use
Energy of the beam
explanation: The source lists anatomical structure, film material and beam energy as influences on exposure-factor choice. The answer is one of those explicitly named factors.

stem: Which joints should an image of the humerus include in the positioning notes?
quote: Rest the hmerus against the film to include shoulder and elbow.
explanation: The humerus section instructs inclusion of shoulder and elbow. This question uses that unambiguous coverage statement rather than the slide's inconsistent subsection heading.

stem: What centring point is specified for the AP humerus in the humerus section?
options: Anterior humerus midway between shoulder and elbow
quote: CP: Anterior aspect of the humerus midway between the shoulder and elbow joints
explanation: The humerus section centres on the anterior aspect midway between shoulder and elbow. Both the anatomical region and midpoint are stated in the source.

stem: For the lateral arm projection, which way is the trunk rotated?
options: Towards the affected side until the chest covers the arm
quote: Rotate trunk away from the affected side until lateral aspect of the humerus rest on the film
explanation: The lateral arm instructions rotate the trunk away from the affected side until the lateral humerus rests on the film. The same section requires inclusion of shoulder and elbow.

stem: Which surface of the foot contacts the film for the dorsiplantar toe projection?
quote: Place plantar aspect of the affected foot on film
explanation: The dorsiplantar toe positioning instructions place the plantar aspect of the affected foot on the film. The patient is seated with knees flexed.

stem: Which set of projections is listed for the toes?
options: PA, ball-catcher and axial carpal tunnel
AP humerus, lateral humerus and inferosuperior
AP elbow, lateral elbow and axial elbow
quote:
Dorsiplantar (anteroposterior)
Dorsiplantar (anteroposterior)Oblique
Lateral
explanation: The toe section lists dorsiplantar, dorsiplantar oblique and lateral projections. These are the projections to identify from this supplied slide.

stem: For the lateral toe projection, which side does the patient lie on?
options: Supine with no hip or knee flexion
quote: Lie the patient on the X-ray couch on the affected side with the hip and knee flexed
explanation: The lateral toe description places the patient on the affected side with hip and knee flexed. The unaffected leg is then placed comfortably in front or behind.

stem: How is the knee supported when placing the toes in a true lateral position?
quote: Place the foot in the true lateral position with the knee raised on a pad and the film under the toes
explanation: The lecture describes a true lateral foot position with the knee raised on a pad and film under the toes. This is the support arrangement stated for lateral toes.

stem: What angle does the plantar surface make with the cassette for the oblique toe position described?
quote: From the AP position, the affected limb is allowed to lean medially to bring the plantar surface of the foot approximately 45 degrees to the cassete
explanation: The oblique toe position is obtained by medial leaning until the plantar surface is approximately 45 degrees to the cassette. The source describes a supporting pad of the same angle.

stem: Which support is specified for the oblique toe position?
options: Metal block under the examined toes
quote: A 45 degree non-radiopaque pad placed under the side of the foot for support with opposite leg acting as a support.
explanation: The lecture specifies a 45-degree non-radiopaque pad under the side of the foot, with the opposite leg also providing support. This is the arrangement described in the notes.

stem: For the dorsiplantar foot position, how are the patient's knees arranged?
options: Flexed while seated on the couch
quote: Patient seat on the X-ray couch with knees flexed
explanation: The foot section places the patient seated on the X-ray couch with knees flexed. The next instruction places the plantar aspect of the affected foot on the film.

stem: Where is the dorsiplantar foot projection centred in the supplied lecture?
options: Dorsum of the foot at the cuboid-navicular region
quote: CP: Dorsum of the foot to the Cubiod-navicular region
explanation: The source gives the cuboid-navicular region on the dorsum of the foot as the centring point. The answer follows the named region in the supplied notes.

stem: Which movement changes the AP foot position into the oblique foot position described?
options: Rotate the limb laterally through 90 degrees
Flex all toes into the sole
Keep the plantar surface flat without rotation
quote: From the AP position, the affected limb is allowed to lean medially to bring the plantar surface of the foot approximately 45 degrees to the cassete
explanation: The oblique foot instructions use medial leaning to bring the plantar surface to approximately 45 degrees. This tests the direction of movement given in the lecture.

stem: In the lateral foot notes, when is a horizontal central ray specifically mentioned?
options: With the cassette lateral to the foot in pes planus
quote: DCR:: Vertical or Horizontal (if cassette is placed at the lateral part of the foot in case of pes planus[Flat foot])
explanation: The lateral foot description explicitly mentions a horizontal ray with a laterally placed cassette in pes planus. The question stays within that stated example.

stem: For the AP ankle position, how should the malleoli relate to the couch top?
options: Both should be equidistant from it
Only the medial malleolus should be imaged
Both should lie outside the cassette
quote: Rotate the ankle medially until both malleoli are equidistant from the couch top.
explanation: The AP ankle instructions require medial rotation until the malleoli are equidistant from the couch top. This is the alignment stated for that projection.

stem: Where is the AP ankle projection centred in the notes?
quote: CP: Midway between the malleoli
explanation: The AP ankle centring point is midway between the malleoli. The separate lateral ankle section on the next slide uses the medial malleolus.

stem: Which relationship of the malleoli is specified for the lateral ankle?
options: Malleoli equidistant with no lateral rotation
quote: Place the affected ankle in the true lateral position such as that both malleoli are superimposed with the knee raised on a pad
explanation: The lateral ankle notes require a true lateral position with superimposed malleoli and the knee raised on a pad. This is the stated alignment check.

stem: What centring landmark is given for the lateral ankle?
quote: CP: Medial malleolus
explanation: The lateral ankle section specifies the medial malleolus as its centring landmark. The AP ankle uses the midpoint between the malleoli instead.

stem: Which joints should be included if possible on an AP tibia-fibula image?
quote: Include both ankle and knee joints on the film if possible.
explanation: The AP leg instructions ask for inclusion of both ankle and knee if possible. This is the source's stated image-coverage requirement for the lower leg.

stem: Where is the AP lower-leg projection centred?
options: Anterior middle of the lower leg between ankle and knee
quote: CP: Anterior aspect of the middle of lower leg midway between the ankle and knee joints
explanation: The AP lower-leg centring point is the anterior midpoint between ankle and knee. It is not the centring point used for an isolated ankle image.

stem: For the AP tibia-fibula position, how is the ankle arranged?
options: Flexed 90 degrees with the foot upright
Fully plantarflexed with toes pointing down
Rotated until only the heel is visible
quote: Place the lower leg on the film-cassette with the ankle joint flexed 90 degrees with foot upright.
explanation: The AP leg description specifies an ankle flexed 90 degrees with the foot upright. This question tests the position stated in the supplied lecture.

stem: Where is the lateral lower-leg projection centred?
options: Medial aspect of the lower leg midway between ankle and knee
Dorsum of the foot at the metatarsal heads
quote: CP: Medial aspect of the middle of the lower leg midway between the ankle and knee joints.
explanation: The lateral leg centring point is the medial midpoint between ankle and knee. This contrasts with the anterior aspect specified for the AP lower leg.

stem: Which patellar alignment is required for the AP knee position in the lecture?
options: Patella displaced fully lateral to the femur
quote: Ensure that the patella is central over the femur
explanation: The AP knee instructions explicitly require the patella to be central over the femur. This is the positioning check stated in the notes.

stem: Where is the AP knee projection centred according to the notes?
options: 2.5 cm below the apex of the patella
quote: CP: 2.5cm below the apex of the patella
explanation: The AP knee centring point is 2.5 cm below the patellar apex. Both the distance and reference landmark are given on the source slide.

stem: In the PA patella instructions, which patient position is described?
options: Prone with the knee slightly flexed
Supine with the knee fully extended
Standing with both hands on the cassette
Seated with the ankle crossed over the opposite knee
quote: Patient lie prone on the table with knee slightly flexed
explanation: The PA patella section specifies a prone patient with slight knee flexion. The question refers to that section rather than the lateral knee section above it.

stem: Where are foam pads placed for the PA patella position described?
quote: Foam pads are placed under the ankle and thigh for support
explanation: The PA patella positioning instructions place foam pads beneath the ankle and thigh for support. Those two support sites are explicitly named in the source.

stem: Where is the PA patella projection centred in the lecture?
options: Midline at the skin crease behind the knee
Anterior middle of the tibial shaft
quote: CP: In the midline to the skin crease behind the knee
explanation: The PA patella instructions give the midline skin crease behind the knee as the centring point. This differs from the AP knee landmark on the preceding slide.

stem: For the lateral knee, where is the unaffected leg placed in the positioning notes?
options: Comfortably in front of the affected leg
Directly on top of the affected knee
quote: Rest the unaffected leg in a comfortable position in front of  the affected leg.
explanation: The lateral knee description places the unaffected leg comfortably in front of the affected leg. The remaining steps establish a true lateral knee position and immobilization.
